business_summary.text: Filatex India Limited is a manufacturer of polyester yarns, with a focus on FDY, POY, and DTY segments. The company is undergoing a strategic transition with investments in value-added products, textile-to-textile chemical recycling through its subsidiary Ecosis, automation, and renewable energy.

call_points.text: Ecosis has 15-20% of production committed with Decathlon and another undisclosed brand
Margins stabilized after April lows; inventory gains of ₹15-17 Cr in Q1FY27
Geopolitical risks remain key concern; India's MEG import dependency is a structural risk
FY27 revenue seen at about ₹4,500 Cr, with only six months of new production; FY28 at ₹4,800 Cr plus ₹400 Cr from Ecosis.
Steam project delayed by about a month to mid-July due to turbine delivery; recycling plant on track for end-September.
March and current spreads are EBITDA-neutral; Q3FY26 profitability was around ₹9/kg.
Petrochemical input costs rose 40-45% due to crude volatility; weak demand limited pass-through.
Industry running at around 60% capacity utilisation; Filatex at around 75%.
Five capex projects are underway including Ecosis recycling and brownfield PFY expansion.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Joint Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, Vadodara has issued Show Cause Notice dated 14.6.2023 proposing to recover GST refund claims of Rs. 74.59 Crores of inverted duty structure for the period January 2018 to October 2019 (except December 2018) on the ground of alleged erroneous refunds which were granted by Assistant Commissioner Bharuch under Rule 89(5) of the CGST Rules. The Company has filed a writ petition with the Hon'ble Gujarat High Court against the order of Joint Commissioner of CGST. The Hon'ble Gujarat High Court has stayed the matter vide its order dated 04.08.2023.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, Vadodara II
tax_litigation.status: The Hon'ble Gujarat High Court has quashed and set aside the said show cause notices vide its judgement dated 28th November, 2025. The Company received certified copies of the said judgement on 4th December, 2025. In this regard, the Company infomed the stock exchanges on 4th December, 2025.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Joint Commissioner CGST has issued Show Cause Notice No V/GST/II/FILATEX/VAD-II/2023-24 dated 21.09.2023 and sought to recover sanctioned GST refunds of Inverted Duty Structure, of Rs. 92.20 Crores for the period November 2019 to February 2022 (excluding month of August 2020, May 2021, October 2021 and December 2021). The Company has filed the Writ Petition on 05.10.2023 with Gujarat High Court at Ahmedabad against the Show Cause Notice. Ad Interim Stay has been granted.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, Vadodara II
tax_litigation.status: The Hon'ble Gujarat High Court has quashed and set aside the said show cause notices vide its judgement dated 28th November, 2025. The Company received certified copies of the said judgement on 4th December, 2025. In this regard, the Company infomed the stock exchanges on 4th December, 2025.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Income-Tax Department had conducted a search under section 132 of the Income-Tax Act, 1961 at the business premises of the Company on September 01, 2021. Subsequently, the Company has received Income tax demand dated 31.03.2022 of Rs. 44.45 Crores (including interest) for AY 2016-17. The Company has preferred an appeal against the said demand. The company verily believes that there is a fair chance of decision going in its favour, which is based on an expert's opinion, hence no provision is considered necessary against the same.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (DCIT), Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The Commissioner appeals has set aside the entire demand and decided the case in favour of the company vide order in appeal No. DIN: ITBA/GEA/M/2024-25/1064344173(1) dated 25.04.2024. However, the department has gone in appeal with ITAT against the order of the Commissioner Appeals.Appeal filed by the department with ITAT Delhi has been dismissed vide ITAT Delhi order dated 30.06.2025. The Department has preferred an appeal in Delhi High Court. The appeal is yet to be admitted.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For AY 2021-22, the Company has received Income tax demand dated 30.12.2022 of Rs. 22.77 Crores (including interest and as revised vide rectification order dated 27.05.2023) from the Income tax department. The Company has preferred an appeal against the same. The company verily believes that there is a fair chance of decision going in its favour, which is based on an expert's opinion, hence no provision is considered necessary against the same.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (DCIT), Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The Commissioner appeals (CIT (Appeal)) vide its order in appeal DIN: ITBA/APL/M/250/2023-24/1060519927(1) dated 05.02.2024 has reduced the demand from 22.77 Crores to Rs 1.86 Crores. The Company has filed rectification application with CIT(A) for deletion of demand of Rs 1.86 crores due to error in computation of the same. Also, the CIT (Appeal) has proposed the addition of Rs. 1.50 Crores in taxable income for which tax liability is yet to be finalised by the CIT (Appeals). The company has filed appeal with ITAT, Delhi against the said addition. The department has gone in appeal with ITAT against the order of the CIT (Appeal).Appeal filed by the department with ITAT Delhi has been dismissed and the appeal of the company against the addition of 1.50 crore has been allowed vide ITAT Delhi order dated 30.06.2025. The Department has preferred an appeal in Delhi High Court. The appeal is yet to be admitted.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: DCIT has confirmed demand of Income Tax along with interest Rs 42.15 Crores wide order-in-original no. ITBA/AST/S/186/2024-25/1065711414(1) dated 14.06.2024 in respect of certain addition and disallowances in AY 2018-19. Appeal against the order of DCIT has been filed with Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) on 21.06.2024. The next date of hearing is awaited. In view of the favourable order received from CIT (Appeals) in earlier financial year in similar matter, the Company does not expect the said order to have any material financial impact.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax (DCIT), Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The Commissioner appeals (CIT (Appeal)) vide its order in appeal DIN: ITBA/APL/S/250/2025-26/1085082780(1) dated 22.01.2026 has deleted the demand of Rs. 42.15 crore. The department has preferred an appeal with ITAT against the order of the CIT (Appeal). The Company will file cross objection against the said appeal in due course.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹985.49 Cr (-8.8% YoY), net profit ₹40.08 Cr (-2.5% YoY).
Filatex India released its Q4 FY26 investor presentation highlighting capex progress and circular recycling MoUs.
Filatex India Limited shared the audio recording of its Q4 & FY26 earnings conference call on 4th May 2026 via its website.
Filatex India held its Q4 & FY26 earnings call on 4 May 2026, guiding FY27 revenue to about ₹4,500 Cr and detailing a ₹690 Cr capex programme.
On 12 May 2026, Filatex India announced an additional ₹10 Cr investment in its wholly owned subsidiary Ecosis Limited via a rights issue.
On 12 May 2026, Filatex India informed the exchange that India Ratings & Research reaffirmed its credit ratings on bank facilities totaling ₹998 Cr.
Filatex India informed the exchange that India Ratings reaffirmed the IND A+/Stable rating on the ₹200 Cr term loan of subsidiary Ecosis Limited.

Filatex India Limited held Q1FY27 earnings conference call on 31 July 2026, reporting 16.3% QoQ revenue growth to ₹1,145 Cr and 22.1% QoQ PAT growth to ₹49.1 Cr, with updates on capex progress and Ecosis recycling plant launch.
